title: Cron job to queue: what broke first
receipt: Migrated a nightly cron job to a work queue with retries; failed runs dropped about 40% in the first two weeks.
why_now: Two weeks of data is in, and queue-vs-cron is a recurring argument on most teams.
questions: What failed the night you decided the cron job had to go?
What did you expect the queue to fix that it didn't?
If a teammate asked tomorrow, would you tell them to do the same, and why?

title: The dashboard nobody opened
receipt: Deleted a reporting dashboard after the view logs showed 3 opens in 90 days, and replaced it with one weekly summary message.
why_now: Quarter planning is when teams commission new dashboards.
questions: What made you check the view logs in the first place?
Who pushed back when you proposed deleting it, and what did they say?
What does the weekly summary tell people that the dashboard never did?

title: Tests before the refactor, not after
receipt: Wrote 22 characterization tests before refactoring a billing module; two of them caught behavior nobody had documented.
why_now: Fresh from the refactor; the two surprises are still vivid.
questions: What were the two behaviors the tests caught, in plain words?
Where do you think this advice is wrong or overkill?
What would have happened if you had skipped the tests?

title: Reading a vendor benchmark like a skeptic
receipt: Re-ran a vendor's published latency benchmark on our own workload and got numbers about 3x slower.
questions: What was different between their test setup and your workload?
Which number would you actually use in a decision, and why?
What is one question you now ask every vendor benchmark?

title: Onboarding doc rewritten from new-hire questions
receipt: Collected every question a new teammate asked in week one and rebuilt the onboarding doc around them.
questions: What did you cut from the old doc, and did anyone miss it?
How will you know if the new version works?
